headline: Nigerian Crude Shipments to US Drop 58% as Local Refinining Rises
summary: Nigeria’s crude oil shipments to the United States fell 57.8 percent in the first eight months of the year amid rising domestic crude intake by Dangote.
why: Shifts in domestic crude processing reorient trade flows, reducing export volumes to traditional western buyers while altering feedstock availability for regional refiners.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Lower crude shipments from Nigeria reduce available imported West African feedstock for US refiners.

why_moved: Diverting crude supplies to domestic refineries curtails export quotas, reducing international delivery volumes to key importing nations.
